description:
Surfaced 2026-05-12 by project-tier POLYBIUS via HUMAN_relay_substrate_bw_scaling_findings_2026-05-12.md. Two feedback-shaped memories saved at workspace tier during the bw → Ariadne integration arc; both apply broadly across Stoa-team projects and are candidates for substrate-tier replication.

## Two memories to consider replicating upward

### 1. feedback_fork_over_upstream_issue.md

The AI-team OSS calculus is inverted from human-dev convention. For a human dev team, fork-and-tailor is expensive (maintenance burden, drift from upstream, sync cost); upstream-issue-filing is cheap (open ticket, wait, maybe land). For an AI agent team, fork-and-tailor is cheap (the agent can carry the diff trivially; sync is also automatable); upstream-issue-filing is expensive coordination overhead (write the issue, wait, possibly never resolved, blocks the project).

**Default for AI-team projects: fork-and-tailor when the dep does not fit our specific use case. Upstream-contribute-back is optional and post-hoc.**

The 2026-05-12 bw arc validates this empirically: a 150 LOC TreeFS-incremental-tree-update patch is a small fork-and-tailor surface for the AI team but a substantial upstream coordination job (RFC, jallum review, possibly multiple rounds, possibly rejected for design-fit reasons). Project tier chose pivot-the-use-case rather than fork the dep, but the architectural option to fork was always cheap and on the table.

### 2. project_agent_time_latency_budget.md

100% of Ariadne traffic is agent-to-system; the latency budget is per-LLM-turn (5-20s acceptable), not per-human-keystroke (<1s expected). Optimizing for human-perceived-instant response is over-optimization for a system that wont be touched by human keystrokes.

This shifts engineering decisions on several axes:
- 1-2s synchronous ingest API call: acceptable (vs unacceptable in human-facing system)
- Bulk operations spread over minutes: acceptable
- Async-queue-for-bulk: not needed unless wall-clock becomes a real bottleneck
- UI polish / streaming responses: lower priority than correctness/coverage

Worth knowing for any substrate-deployed project that has the same agent-vs-human-consumer split.

## Substrate touch-points

Probably operating-disciplines.md gains two short sections — one on fork-over-upstream default, one on agent-time latency budget. Could also live as canonical-memory files referenced from there.

Substrate memory canon location: TBD. Currently this substrate has no explicit memory-canon mechanism (vs workspace-tier memory files at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/). Either:
- Inline in operating-disciplines.md (simpler)
- New substrate/memory/ directory (more structured; requires the file-references-from-role-files plumbing)

DAEDALUS-light picks the placement; either works.

## Gauntlet

ADA + CATO eyeball if inlined; DAEDALUS-light + ADA + CATO if creating a new substrate/memory/ directory shape.

## Sequencing

P3. Ride with the bw-fit matrix ticket (stoa--vmc) since both are substrate-discipline doc updates.

Project-tier relay 2026-05-12; workspace-tier memory files at ariadne-core-workspace memory dir (replicable upward as the relay names).
